solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New Fiat progresses over time — these provide fillip?

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new Fiat car makes headway over time, and some decoration gives it a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal for FIAT PROGRESSES plus T; 'over' only joins the time letter to the pool. Go-faster stripes are decorative stripes painted on cars, mainly in Britain, to make them look fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative racing stripes are a cosmetic boost, giving a car a touch of extra dash or a fillip.

clue.text: Gore's a huge sense for change — countering these?

definitions.text: Gore's a huge sense for change — countering these?

indicators.note: the words are offered up for change, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: Al Gore, the former US vice-president, is a prominent climate campaigner

explanation.surface: Al Gore has a strong feeling that things must change, and he campaigns against climate pollutants.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Al Gore's climate campaigning is aimed against the very thing the rearranged letters spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide and methane trap heat in the atmosphere and drive climate change, which Gore campaigns against.

clue.text: Celebrating quins is in Paris to be entertained?

indicators.note: the five is to play host to the French word, which goes inside it

parts.note: quins (quintuplets) come in a group of five
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: Quintuplets visiting Paris enjoying a celebration while being entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive mood is a celebratory one, so the adjective fits a party atmosphere as a synonym.

clue.text: Hear corps somehow cultivate land

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen to a military corps as it somehow farms the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm land as a tenant who pays the owner with part of the harvest is a way of cultivating it.

clue.text: Like two, tense, in pole vault maybe

parts.note: two is an even number
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Two athletes, tense, taking part in the pole vault.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is an example of an athletics competition, a single item on the programme of a meeting.

clue.text: Provider of much liquid as art tour moves round

indicators.note: the letters move round into a new order

explanation.surface: Something supplying plenty of drink as an art tour goes round the galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that soaks something completely supplies a great deal of fluid, so it is a provider of much liquid.

clue.text: Matches late in season causing quarrel

definitions.meaning: the final stretch of a sporting season, its closing fixtures

explanation.surface: Late-season games leading to a row between rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing stretch of a season and a squabble are both common senses of the hyphenated noun.

clue.text: One following United introduced to ship's officer

indicators.note: the letter for United is introduced into the officer's title

parts.note: a purser is the officer in charge of a ship's accounts and passengers
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A follower of Manchester United, say, being presented to an officer aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chasing or tracking another is one who follows, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: It provides safety net in Council's areas after redevelopment

indicators.note: the words are redeveloped, rebuilt into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A welfare scheme offered in a council's districts once they have been regenerated.
explanation.definitionFit: State benefits funded by contributions catch people who fall on hard times, the welfare state's safety net.

clue.text: European Union attitude not new for this guy

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for new is left out

parts.note: a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: A man whose views on Europe are old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes N (new) from STANCE, leaving STACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so the clue calls him simply a guy, a fellow.

clue.text: Beat dodge, we hear, referring to some teachings

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: to tan is to beat, and a trick is a dodge

explanation.surface: A way to beat the system, apparently, found in certain doctrines.
explanation.walkthrough: TAN + TRICK said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes Hindu and Buddhist texts and practices called tantras, a body of religious teachings.

clue.text: Too trusting spa town recalled

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the town's name runs backwards

parts.note: Evian is a French spa town known for its bottled water

explanation.surface: Someone too credulous remembering a visit to a spa resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone innocent and credulous trusts too readily, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Spider natural at swimming

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely into a new order

explanation.surface: A spider that takes to the water naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy kind of spider, so the clue names its broader class.

clue.text: Show too much emotion about poor race, ultimately unimportant

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: a poor version of the word is a garbled one, its letters rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone getting worked up about a bad race that hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges RACE into REAC; 'ultimately' takes T from the end of 'unimportant'.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond more strongly than a situation warrants is to show excessive emotion.

clue.text: In clear change, leave port

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Following a clear shift of plan, depart from the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense of 'port' pulls toward sailing, but it is the definition: a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian city on the White Sea, historically the country's chief northern seaport.

clue.text: I'm surprised at soldier's dog

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone surprised by a soldier's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Dance company at start taking in London celebrity

indicators.note: at start takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: a lion is a celebrity, a social lion

explanation.surface: A firm's party at which a famous Londoner is welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' looks like an insertion, but 'at start' takes the first letters of 'taking in London'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century French ballroom dance, so it is a specific example of a dance.

clue.text: Oddly sweet jump that's arranged beforehand

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in the odd positions of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A strangely pleasant leap that was planned in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix or put-up job is something prearranged, so the noun means a thing rigged in advance.

clue.text: Speak badly of exchange involving university clubs

indicators.note: involving means taking the letters inside it

parts.note: trade means exchange
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Bad-mouthing a trade deal between university societies.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign or defame someone is to speak ill of them, a formal synonym.

clue.text: No flexibility in turning up for these chaps initially — sadly some tire

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word before it
sadly signals the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state

explanation.surface: Office workers who must show up at fixed hours, some of whom find it tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Under flexitime, staff may choose their hours except during set periods when everyone must be present.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed hours when attendance is compulsory leave no flexibility about when staff arrive.

clue.text: Give false information to Military Intelligence: deal's off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Deceiving the intelligence services after an agreement collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or lead astray by giving wrong information is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Country celebration in which posh had meal with magnificent starter?

indicators.note: in which puts the following pieces inside the celebration

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
U is the British label for upper-class, posh
ate means had a meal

indicators.note: starter takes the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A party where the upper classes dined, beginning with something splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American republic, so the clue names its category.

clue.text: When I expect to arrive, around six, for musical

indicators.note: around says the arrival time goes around the numeral

parts.note: ETA is the estimated time of arrival
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A theatregoer planning to arrive at about six for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lloyd Webber and Rice stage show about Eva Perón is a well-known musical.

clue.text: Alert watchman from afar, Gustav

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sentry warning Gustav from a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the hundred-eyed giant set to guard Io, so the name means a vigilant guardian.

clue.text: One unsuccessful, more miserly, losing head

indicators.note: losing head drops the opening letter

parts.note: close means stingy, so closer is more miserly

explanation.surface: A failed and increasingly stingy person losing their cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails or comes off worse in a contest is one who is unsuccessful.

clue.text: Being cheeky to seniors and upsetting children is not good at outset

indicators.note: at outset takes the opening letter of each of the seven words before it

explanation.surface: Insolence towards elderly people and upsetting children is a bad start.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone lip or talking back is being impudent, a British colloquial verb sense.

clue.text: African gets old British coin at auction finally

parts.note: a guinea was a British gold coin worth twenty-one shillings

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone acquiring an antique British coin at the end of an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Guinea in West Africa, so the clue names the broader nationality group.

clue.text: Bucket list advice, Italian style?

parts.note: a bucket list names things to do before dying; this Italian proverb urges a visit to a southern Italian city first

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a city on the Bay of Naples is so beautiful that once seen, nothing else in life matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional saying recommending one sight above all others before death, exactly what a bucket list records.
